prose_updates.tldr: On the restrictive component-aligned Gaussian LiMVAM class, the main completion result extends calibration subsets to an arbitrary observed view graph. A candidate common order is compatible exactly when every observed residual cross-block is diagonal and, separately for each variable, the resulting partial disturbance covariance has a positive-definite completion. For chordal view graphs this is the constructive maximal-clique test from the classical positive-definite matrix-completion theorem; a signed four-cycle shows that positive-definite edge blocks alone do not suffice for nonchordal graphs. The earlier calibration-subset certificate is the clique-plus-isolated-vertices special case. Independently, a sharp generic elbow proves that no paired block is insufficient while any one preassigned view pair identifies the full coefficient tuple off one proper algebraic exceptional set. The proved memoized removed-set recursion gives a \(2^p\)-state compatibility representation, while covariance-region inversion provides the finite-sample supporting result under its stated nondegeneracy and margin conditions.

project_justification.gap: Existing multi-view LiMVAM identification results address full pairing under conditions on disturbance diversity, while Gaussian-DAG estimators target a point-identified DAG from one joint law. Neither line characterizes compatibility when cross-view covariances are observed on an arbitrary graph, where diagonal residual restrictions and positive-definite completion are distinct requirements.
project_justification.niche: For the component-aligned Gaussian subclass, a fixed candidate order determines every view-specific coefficient matrix from its marginal covariance. Each observed view edge then fixes entries of the coordinatewise disturbance covariance, so global compatibility becomes a positive-definite partial-matrix completion problem after the observable residual-diagonality test. This separates order testing, global noise feasibility, and coefficient recovery, and it retains every unpaired view marginal for coefficient estimation.
project_justification.fill: The graph-completion theorem proves necessity by restricting any full coordinatewise disturbance covariance to its observed diagonal and edge entries, and proves sufficiency by choosing one positive-definite completion for each variable and assembling independent Gaussian disturbance stacks. On chordal view graphs, the classical completion theorem reduces feasibility to positive definiteness of every maximal specified clique and supplies a constructive certificate. A nonchordal four-cycle with unit diagonals and successive edge correlations \(0.9,0.9,0.9,-0.9\) has positive-definite edge blocks but no positive-semidefinite completion, so edgewise checks alone are not valid in general. The generic calibration elbow separately proves that one observed pair is generically necessary and sufficient. The memoized removed-set DAG preserves the proved \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p)\) compatibility recursion.

prose_updates.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is the flagship model anchor: its Section 4.6 uses edgewise cross-view correlation diversity to identify a partial order and view-specific coefficients under full pairing. The present conclusions are only for the narrower component-aligned Gaussian subclass and do not claim containment of the published Heurtebise class. ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM and Shimizu2012JointLiNGAM motivate recursive residualization under non-Gaussianity, but they do not prove removed-set path independence or partial-view-graph covariance completion. ChenEtAl2024IndividualCausal and GhassamiEtAl2018MultiDomain pool population or domain information through ICA structure or heterogeneity rather than through selected paired cross-covariance blocks. HyttinenEberhardtHoyer2012Overlapping studies overlapping experimental total-effect measurements, not residual covariance restrictions among passive views. The positive-definite completion theorem of Grone, Johnson, S\'a, and Wolkowicz (1984, Theorem 7) supplies the chordal maximal-clique criterion used by the graph specialization; the arbitrary-graph reduction and the signed four-cycle incompatibility example are derived for the present disturbance matrices. HauserBuhlmann2014ActiveLearning and LindgrenEtAl2018CostAware concern intervention-target design through separating systems, whereas the present calibration choice is passive observation of view-pair covariance blocks. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses recursive Schur updates and score gaps in a point-identifying linear SEM. GaoTaiAragam2022GaussianDAG studies point-identifying Gaussian-DAG estimation rather than partial paired-view calibration and set-valued order compatibility. Vershynin2018HighDimensionalProbability supplies Gaussian singular-value concentration used for covariance radii, and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference supplies the general criterion-inversion comparison; neither gives the LiMVAM-specific residual and path-product moduli. MohanPearl2021MissingData studies recoverability under missingness graphs, whereas the present sourcewise-iid common-population sampling design assumes away selection and transport. TaylorEtAl2017CamCAN documents the MEG and MRI cohort that motivates a future diagnostic application, but it does not validate component alignment or the calibration-sampling assumptions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-completion characterization is population-level and remains confined to the component-aligned Gaussian subclass. For nonchordal view graphs, positive definiteness of every specified edge block is only necessary; global completion must still be checked. The generic elbow is relative to a fixed-order finite-dimensional parameterization and supplies no uniform distance from its algebraic exceptional set. Covariance-region inversion requires the selected joint covariance \(\Sigma^{SS}\succ0\) in addition to positive-definite view marginals; this premise is essential for whitening and excludes singular identical-view laws. Its Hausdorff and poset guarantees also require fixed feasibility and path-product margins. The \(2^p\)-state recursion counts exact-real arithmetic rather than bit complexity. Duplicate-free numerical tuple enumeration beyond compatible-order enumeration is not claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The arbitrary-view-graph completion theorem, its chordal specialization, the nonchordal obstruction, the generic calibration elbow, fixed-order recovery, removed-set recursion, essential poset, and covariance-region inversion concern only the component-aligned Gaussian subclass with positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. They do not transfer automatically to unrestricted LiMVAMs or establish the assumptions used by Heurtebise et al. Genericity is relative to coefficients respecting a fixed common order and gives no uniform identification margin. Finite-sample inversion additionally assumes a positive-definite selected joint covariance and sourcewise-iid common-population sampling; selection and transport are outside the model. Cam-CAN MEG and fMRI remain prospective diagnostic applications rather than empirical validation.
